title: Ethiopian Sweet Potato Fries
localName: ስኳር ድንች ጥብስ — Suqar Dinich Tibs
community: Modern Ethiopian street food — the sweet potato vendor
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Sweet Potato Fries — thick-cut sweet potato sticks deep-fried and seasoned with mitmita and salt. The modern Ethiopian street food — the berbere and mitmita tradition applied to the globally familiar French fry format, producing something completely distinct.
longDesc: Sweet potato fries with mitmita seasoning are a modern Ethiopian street food addition — the globally familiar format given an unmistakably Ethiopian character by mitmita and berbere salt. Popular at Addis Ababa's modern food stalls.
ingredients: 4 large orange sweet potatoes — peeled, cut into thick sticks
// Mitmita Salt: 1 tsp salt + ½ tsp mitmita (ETH142)
steps: Fry in batches 4—5 minutes until golden and slightly caramelised.
Drain. Season immediately with mitmita salt.
chefTips: Sweet potato burns faster than white potato — 175°C maximum, not higher.
Season while hot — sticks to the surface.
cookingScience: Sweet potatoes contain much more sugar (naturally occurring fructose and glucose) than white potatoes — this is why they caramelise faster and why the oil temperature must be lower. The Maillard reaction and caramelisation work together to produce the characteristic deep orange-brown crust.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland sweet potatoes — high in beta-carotene, very nutritious.
healthBenefits: More nutritious than white potato fries.
culturalNote: Sweet potato fries with mitmita are the new generation's Ethiopian street food — the fusion of global form and Ethiopian spice tradition that defines the modern Addis Ababa food scene.
